_comment: RATCHET. This file is the list of import cycles Corvus still carries, and it
may only get SHORTER. The fitness test in backend/tests/test_architecture_cycles.py
asserts this list matches the cycles in architecture/architecture.json exactly,
- a cycle in the code that is NOT here fails the gate (no new cycles);
- an entry here that is NO LONGER a cycle also fails (fix it, then delete the
entry — stale entries would let the ratchet slip back up unnoticed).
Raising `budget` is the only way to admit a new cycle, and it is deliberately a
one-line diff in a file named for the debt it tracks, so review cannot miss it.

history.note: Baseline at record 04 seam 1: compliance registry/frameworks/providers (20), governance policies (4), maintenance/reconsolidation cluster (12), executor/pipeline stages (8), neuron_index<->neuron_service (2).

Record 04a retired the compliance context; its 20-module cycle left with it. Not a decoupling win — registry.py imported inside load_all(), so the extractor was counting a plugin registry it could not see through.

Record 04 seam 2: broke neuron_index <-> neuron_service by extracting NeuronCandidate and FRESHNESS_SQL into app/services/neuron_candidate.py, a leaf module with no imports. neuron_index sits UNDER the service and was importing it back for two pieces of shared vocabulary; executor was reaching through the service's privacy for the same SQL. First cycle broken by decoupling rather than by deletion.

Record 04 seam 3: broke the app.governance.policies package-init cycle by extracting PolicyContext, ViolationDraft and the config helpers into policies/base.py. The __init__ defined the base types AND imported the three concrete policies to build POLICY_CLASSES, while each policy imported those types back; the `# noqa: E402` on the bottom imports was the confession. __init__ is now a pure facade, so every external importer is unchanged.
